q: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?
options: Much energy is needed to break covalent bonds within the ions
The ions are very small and light
The compounds contain strong bonds between separate molecules
Much energy is needed to overcome the many strong electrostatic attractions between ions in the lattice
explain: The giant lattice has strong attractions between oppositely charged ions throughout, so a lot of energy is needed to separate them.

q: Which statement describes the structure of silicon(IV) oxide, SiO₂?
options: Separate SiO₂ molecules held by weak forces
A lattice of Si⁴⁺ and O²⁻ ions
Layers of silicon and oxygen atoms with delocalised electrons
A giant covalent lattice in which each silicon atom is bonded to four oxygen atoms
explain: SiO₂ is a giant lattice; each Si bonds to four O atoms and each O to two Si atoms, giving the ratio 1 : 2.

q: Element X has two isotopes, ²⁰X and ²²X, and a relative atomic mass of 20.2. What is the percentage abundance of ²⁰X?
explain: Let x be the fraction of ²⁰X: 20x + 22(1 − x) = 20.2, so 22 − 2x = 20.2 and x = 0.90, i.e. 90%.

q: Why does an aqueous solution of an ionic compound conduct electricity?
options: The ions are free to move through the solution
Electrons flow freely through the water
The ions are held in a regular lattice
The compound forms molecules in water
explain: When dissolved, the lattice breaks apart and the ions move freely, carrying the current.

q: What happens when an atom forms a negative ion (anion)?
options: It loses one or more electrons
It gains one or more protons
It gains one or more electrons
It loses one or more neutrons
explain: An anion has more electrons than protons because the atom has gained electrons.

q: Which property is different for two isotopes of the same element?
options: Their mass (and density)
Their number of outer electrons
Their proton number
Their reaction with oxygen
explain: Different neutron numbers change the mass, so physical properties such as density differ, while electrons and chemistry stay the same.

q: Which row correctly describes pure liquid hydrogen chloride (HCl)?
options: ionic | conducts
covalent | does not conduct
covalent | conducts
ionic | does not conduct
explain: Hydrogen and chlorine share electrons (covalent bonding); the HCl molecules are uncharged so the liquid does not conduct.

q: Sodium atoms each have one outer electron. How many delocalised electrons does solid sodium have for each sodium atom?
explain: Each atom contributes its one outer electron to the sea, forming Na⁺ ions in the lattice.

q: Boron has two isotopes: ¹⁰B (20%) and ¹¹B (80%). What is the relative atomic mass of boron?
An atom has proton number 11 and mass number 23. How many neutrons does it contain?
explain: Neutrons = mass number − proton number = 23 − 11 = 12.

q: Which compound consists of simple molecules?
options: Methane, CH₄
Sodium chloride, NaCl
Magnesium oxide, MgO
Potassium bromide, KBr
explain: Methane has carbon and hydrogen atoms joined by covalent bonds into small molecules. The others are ionic.

q: How many hydrogen atoms are covalently bonded to the nitrogen atom in one molecule of ammonia?
explain: Nitrogen needs three more electrons for a full outer shell, so it forms three bonds, one to each of three hydrogen atoms.

q: Which compound contains ionic bonds?
options: Methane, CH₄
Hydrogen chloride, HCl
Potassium bromide, KBr
Ammonia, NH₃
explain: Potassium (metal) transfers an electron to bromine (non-metal), forming ions. The others contain only non-metals joined by covalent bonds.

q: Which molecule contains a triple bond?
options: O₂
CO₂
N₂
C₂H₄
explain: Nitrogen shares three pairs of electrons. O₂, CO₂ and C₂H₄ each contain double bonds only.

q: Which pair of properties is typical of ionic compounds?
options: High melting point and conduct electricity when molten
Low melting point and conduct electricity when solid
High melting point and conduct electricity when solid
Low melting point and conduct electricity when molten
explain: Strong bonds give a high melting point; the ions can move when molten, but cannot when fixed in the solid.

q: Which is the best description of an ionic bond?
options: A strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
A shared pair of electrons between two atoms
An attraction between positive ions and delocalised electrons
A weak attraction between neutral molecules
explain: Ionic bonding is the electrostatic attraction between positive and negative ions. Sharing electrons is covalent bonding.

q: Does molten metal conduct electricity?
options: No, because the lattice has broken down
No, because the ions are fixed
Yes, but only because the ions carry the current
Yes, because delocalised electrons can still move
explain: Metallic bonding persists in the liquid, so delocalised electrons still carry the current.

q: Which formula represents a compound?
options: N₂
O₂
Cl₂
CO
explain: CO contains two different elements, carbon and oxygen, chemically bonded. The others each contain only one element.

q: Which atom has the greatest number of neutrons?
options: ³⁵₁₇Cl
²⁷₁₃Al
³⁷₁₇Cl
²⁴₁₂Mg
explain: Neutrons: Cl-37 has 20, Cl-35 has 18, Al-27 has 14 and Mg-24 has 12.

q: In a molecule of methanol, CH₃OH, how many pairs of electrons are shared in total?
explain: Three C–H bonds, one C–O bond and one O–H bond are all single bonds, giving 5 shared pairs.

q: Why do simple molecular substances have low melting and boiling points?
options: The forces between the molecules are weak and need little energy to overcome
The covalent bonds within each molecule are weak
The molecules contain few atoms
The molecules are held in a lattice by strong ionic attractions
explain: Melting separates whole molecules, which needs little energy because the intermolecular forces are weak.

q: Why does diamond not conduct electricity?
options: It contains ions that are fixed in position
It is too hard for charge to flow
It has no free electrons because all outer electrons are used in bonds
Its electrons are delocalised but cannot move
explain: Each carbon atom uses all four outer electrons in covalent bonds, so no mobile charged particles exist.

q: How many electrons and neutrons are in the ion ³⁵₁₇Cl⁻?
options: 17 electrons and 18 neutrons
18 electrons and 18 neutrons
18 electrons and 35 neutrons
16 electrons and 18 neutrons
explain: The ion has 17 protons plus one extra electron = 18 electrons. Neutrons = 35 − 17 = 18.

q: What is the electronic configuration of a magnesium atom (proton number 12)?
explain: 12 electrons fill the first shell with 2, the second with 8, leaving 2 in the third shell.

q: A magnesium atom (2,8,2) forms an ion. Which ion is formed?
options: Mg²⁻, by gaining two electrons
Mg²⁺, by losing two electrons
Mg⁺, by losing one electron
Mg²⁺, by gaining two protons
explain: Losing the 2 outer electrons gives the stable configuration 2,8 and a charge of 2+.

q: What happens when liquid methane boils?
options: The covalent bonds within molecules break
The ions separate from one another
The molecules split into carbon and hydrogen atoms
The weak forces between molecules are overcome
explain: Methane has a low boiling point because only weak intermolecular forces need to be overcome; the covalent bonds stay intact.

q: An element has the electronic configuration 2,8,3. In which group and period is it found?
options: Group III, Period 8
Group I, Period 3
Group III, Period 2
Group III, Period 3
explain: Three outer electrons give Group III and three occupied shells give Period 3 (this element is aluminium).

q: What happens when an atom forms a positive ion (cation)?
options: It loses one or more electrons
It gains one or more electrons
It loses one or more protons
It gains one or more protons
explain: A cation has more protons than electrons because the atom has lost electrons; the number of protons never changes in ion formation.

q: Which statement describes the structure of graphite?
options: Layers of carbon atoms, each atom bonded to three others, with weak forces between the layers
A lattice in which each carbon atom is bonded to four others
Small molecules of carbon held by weak forces
A lattice of carbon ions in a sea of electrons
explain: Graphite has hexagonal layers of covalently bonded carbon atoms; the layers are held together only weakly.

q: Which row correctly shows whether sodium chloride conducts electricity?
options: conducts | conducts | does not conduct
does not conduct | does not conduct | conducts
conducts | does not conduct | does not conduct
does not conduct | conducts | conducts
explain: Solid NaCl has fixed ions and does not conduct; molten and aqueous NaCl have mobile ions and conduct.
